memory_update.text: Primary Layer 1B direct universe for enterprise AI agents/data/workflow automation: MSFT, CRM, NOW, PLTR, SNOW.

The software chokepoint appears to cluster around governed workflow execution, systems-of-record context, identity/permissions, data quality, auditability, and observability rather than raw LLM access alone.

Follow-up pass should evaluate second-order or adjacent names not included due to the five-candidate limit: ORCL, SAP, DDOG, CRWD, PANW, TEAM, ADBE, INTU, MDB, WDAY, APPF, RXT, and vertical workflow vendors.

Datadog and CrowdStrike have strong AI observability/security-agent angles, but were excluded from the top-five direct platform list because this pass prioritized enterprise systems-of-record, data platforms, and workflow owners.

Later layers should separate AI revenue with disclosed ARR or usage metrics from AI branding. Key tests: incremental ARR, paid-seat conversion, consumption growth, net retention, AI gross-margin drag, implementation cycle length, and customer ROI evidence.

For the enterprise AI agents/data/workflow node, prioritize NOW, CRM, SNOW, OKTA, and DDOG as a balanced software-chokepoint basket: workflow execution, CRM/customer data, data foundation, agent identity, and observability/security.

The strongest software bottleneck evidence points to governed deployment layers rather than frontier model access alone: AI Control Tower/workflow fabric, Agentforce/Data 360, AI Data Cloud/Cortex, AI-agent identity governance, and AI observability/security.

PLTR remains a high-relevance candidate for later layers because Q1 2026 revenue growth and U.S. commercial growth are strong, but the five-name limit in this pass favored diversified chokepoint roles across workflow, data, identity, and observability.

Additional names to test in later passes: PATH for deterministic agentic automation, TEAM for Jira/Rovo developer workflow agents, WDAY for HR/finance agent system-of-record exposure, CRWD/PANW for agentic SOC and AI security, MDB for operational AI data/vector search, ORCL/SAP/MSFT for enterprise systems of record.

Add TEAM as a high-priority workflow-context candidate for enterprise AI agents because Rovo plus Teamwork Graph may become a governed context/action layer across Jira, Confluence, ITSM, and service workflows.

Add WDAY as a vertical system-of-record candidate for HR and finance agents; evidence should focus on AI actions, agent monetization, and whether AI improves workflow value rather than just product packaging.
Add ESTC as a retrieval/search/observability infrastructure candidate for production AI agents, especially where enterprise RAG, logs, and security telemetry are required.
IBM should be tracked as the public-market wrapper for Confluent's real-time governed data-streaming chokepoint after the acquisition, with emphasis on hybrid environments and AI-agent data flows.

Need a later layer to compare AI monetization quality across candidates: paid AI seats, AI ARR, consumption credits, cloud ARR expansion, net retention, agent workflow execution volume, and gross-margin impact.
